name: Conopophagidae
description: Gnateaters are small, plump, short-tailed birds of the Neotropical forest understory. They are named for their insectivorous diet and spend most of their time foraging close to the ground.

children.name: Conopophaga
children.description: Conopophaga is the primary genus of gnateaters, found in lowland and montane forests across South America.

children.name: Conopophaga ardesiaca
children.description: The slaty gnateater (Conopophaga ardesiaca) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae.

children.name: Conopophaga aurita
children.description: The chestnut-belted gnateater (Conopophaga aurita) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae, the gnateaters. It is found in the Amazon Basin of northern Brazil, southern Colombia and eastern Peru and Ecuador; also the Guianan countries of Guyana, Suriname and eastern French Guiana. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Conopophaga castaneiceps
children.description: The chestnut-crowned gnateater (Conopophaga castaneiceps) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Conopophaga cearae
children.description:
The Ceará Gnateater or Caatinga Gnateater (Conopophaga cearae) is a passerine bird of the gnateater family, Conopophagidae. It is found in forest understory and bushes in northeastern Brazil.
The Ceara Gnateater is locally called "chupa-dente", or "tooth-sucker" in Portuguese due to the sound it produces when it vocalizes.

children.name: Conopophaga lineata
children.description: The rufous gnateater (Conopophaga lineata) is a passerine bird of the gnateater family, Conopophagidae.

children.name: Conopophaga melanogaster
children.description: The black-bellied gnateater (Conopophaga melanogaster) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae. It is endemic to Brazil.

children.name: Conopophaga melanops
children.description: The black-cheeked gnateater (Conopophaga melanops) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae endemic to Brazil. The male is distinguished by its orange crown, black face and white throat, while the female has brown plumage.

children.name: Conopophaga melanoptera
children.description: A gnateater with black cheek from the Andes of Peru and Bolivia.

children.name: Conopophaga peruviana
children.description: The ash-throated gnateater (Conopophaga peruviana) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Conopophaga roberti
children.description: The hooded gnateater (Conopophaga roberti) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae.

children.name: Pittasoma
children.description: Pittasoma — a genus of gnateaters in the family Conopophagidae.

children.name: Pittasoma rufopileatum
children.description: The rufous-crowned antpitta or rufous-crowned pittasoma (Pittasoma rufopileatum) is a species of bird in the gnateater family, Conopophagidae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.
